dct_description_sm: The building of this bibliographic database of Inuit-specific climate change references was a continuation of previous work of a report of What we know, dont know, and need to know about climate change in Inuit Nunangat. The previous report was originated and focused on academic perspectives, and peer-reviewed journal publications which were missing a lot of Inuit-generated concepts surrounding climate change.  Although Inuit academics are increasing, most information about Inuit is originated and conducted by non-Inuit. Very few research projects are Inuit driven research ideas. Also, Inuit perspectives in academia as generated by Inuit themselves are also very rare. It was apparent that focussing on academic publications was simply not adequately capturing the whole perspective. It was decided to conduct a broader search of literature and information not available through academic journal databases. This search focused around Inuit organizations, individuals, and public and private institutions which have interests in the Arctic and Canadian Inuit. These included government reports, private publications like magazines, published interviews and media appearances to name a few. The citations for these sources of literature have been gathered according to specific search criteria. This bibliography is provided to the public in order to make increase the awareness of Inuit-specific perspectives on this topic.

dct_title_s: Inuit-specific climate change bibliography of literature outside of academic reports
